drafting.who: an AI agent (Claude, this project's implementation model family) running as a separate sealed agent
drafting.what_it_could_see: only the sealed packet: catalog facts, the episode format, the authoring rules, a standalone check tool and, from round 1, the owner's review files. No repository, no planner code, no evaluation result.
drafting.packet_built_by: a separate agent that could read the repository, and drafted nothing; its check.py agreed with the repository's pool and label tools on the 16 developer episodes and 80 synthetic ones (0 mismatches)

independence.held: the drafting agent never saw the systems, their code or any result
not_held: Round 0: where a label came out against the quota, the drafter rewrote the scenario under the same id and accepted the new label, which is iteration against the drawn pools.
Three review rounds guided revisions. The owner's notes concern wording, realism and design, never system behaviour.
Round 1: at the owner's request 5 accepted feasible episodes (013, 020, 030, 043, 048) were made infeasible, to keep about a quarter infeasible after the budget category became feasible-only.

The implementation agent (the one that builds the product) read every episode's request and gold while building the owner's review pages and running the verification, so the set is not unseen by the implementer. No product change was made between the freeze and the first run. Any later product change that targets a request form this set contains (for example shape changes naming several days) must be disclosed in the report of every run made after it, and that run reported as 'after looking'.
independence.incident: Round 2: while backing up its own draft, the drafting agent wrote a copy of episodes.json to /tmp, outside its sealed output directory, and deleted it at once. It read nothing outside the packet; the packet digests were unchanged. The rule was restated for round 3, where it wrote only inside output/.
independence.pools_and_labels: candidate pools are drawn by a script from the episode, and every label is proven from catalog facts by tools that run no system under test; neither the drafter nor the reviewer chose them

budget_decision: Proving that a realistic budget is impossible needs the exact cheapest week under whole packages. The exact CP-SAT meal solver could not prove it at realistic amounts (on a developer episode it proved S$25 impossible but settled nothing from S$40 to S$80), so the owner chose feasible, tight budgets (round 1), at least S$2.50 per person per planned meal (round 2). The set therefore has no infeasible budget episode, and its budget episodes are small households or few planned meals.
infeasible_mix: 13 infeasible, all by a slot with no valid meal; 7 of them (013, 020, 024, 027, 029, 030, 043) through a time limit. Attempts to make safety or meals-per-day scenarios infeasible by allergies alone came out feasible and were left feasible.

rounds.what: 60 episodes drafted from the sealed packet
